take:
Every MediaPipe post here is also a TouchDesigner post: TouchDesigner appears in all 6 of them. Creators are not calling the library from code; they use @blankensmithing's MediaPipe plugin inside TouchDesigner, which @neles0n tests on camera and a commenter calls "just built different" ([plugin test](/e/DFaChZeMdn1)). The main use is hand and body tracking as a live controller. In @pepepepebrick's spider piece, hand positions move two creatures across a generated 3D web, and leg count and distance feed pitch and waveform in VCV Rack, so one tracking feed drives both image and sound ([spider web synth](/e/DW6tpWWMtZV)).

Other entries extend that tracking. A compiled guide pairs MediaPipe body tracking for interactive dance art with 3D scanning and Gaussian splats ([creative coding guide](/e/891906d4212e)), and @gerrylistudio's R&D piece, reposted by @touchdesigner, combines MediaPipe with 3D Gaussian Splatting and is labelled not a finished work ([presence study](/e/DYpRWC1OO0u)). At DATLAB, @blankensmithing and @dotsimulate show free components that train classifiers on CHOP data such as gestures, image embeddings or EEG signals; they compare the idea to Google's Teachable Machine and say the classifier itself is a search algorithm, not machine learning ([Classifier TOX](/e/DYaNXZJx_L3)).

The evidence is thin: six posts, several of them silent, and none covering setup problems, latency or tracking accuracy. @ojrgb's caption adds a note of caution about AI-assisted shortcuts flattening what is a deep craft ([mixed feelings](/e/DXOWz4yjN--)). The step-by-step version lives in [the MediaPipe to TouchDesigner pipeline](/guides/mediapipe-touchdesigner-pipeline). It suits creative coders and installation artists who want camera-based hand and body input inside a real-time patch.
